locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how DispatchService records its match latency and outcome metrics? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: There is no defect. Both metrics are recorded in the finally block, so every call (match, no drivers, rider cancel, timeout or thrown error) is counted and timed exactly once. Label values are bounded: region is collapsed to five known codes or "other", and outcome is a fixed union, so series count cannot grow with riders or rides. Latency uses a monotonic clock (hrtime.bigint), and the timeout and abort listener are cleaned up in the same finally block.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A new market launches with regionCode " PDX ". What series does a dispatch there contribute to?
choices: A new series labeled region=" PDX "
No series; the observation is dropped
choiceQuestions.explanation: regionLabel trims and lowercases to "pdx", but that is not in KNOWN_REGIONS, so it returns "other". No new series is created and nothing is dropped. Region is never used raw, so " PDX " cannot appear.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The matcher throws a network error while the rider is still waiting. What is recorded and returned?
choices: Nothing is recorded because the exception skips the metrics code
outcome="error" is recorded with its latency, and the error is rethrown
outcome="no_drivers" is recorded and null is returned
outcome="error" is recorded and null is returned
choiceQuestions.explanation: In the catch block riderSignal is not aborted, so outcome becomes "error" and the error is rethrown. The finally block still runs and records latency and the counter. Null is only returned on rider cancellation.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Why is process.hrtime.bigint() used instead of Date.now() for the latency measurement?
choices: It is monotonic, so wall-clock adjustments (NTP) cannot produce negative or skewed durations
It is required for Histogram.observe to accept the value
It makes the measurement exclude time spent awaiting the matcher
It automatically converts the duration to seconds
choiceQuestions.explanation: hrtime is a monotonic high-resolution clock, so clock steps cannot distort durations. Histogram.observe accepts any number; the code converts nanoseconds to seconds itself by dividing by 1e9; and the measurement deliberately includes the matcher await.
